# TIME AT THE TABLE

## Exhibition
- Venue: Riverside Community House
- Dates: 7–28 November 2026
- Exhibition title: TIME AT THE TABLE
- Descriptor: Everyday work, shared food
- Subject: household vegetable fermentation on Mill Lane
- Typical visit: 5–8 minutes
- Simultaneous visitors: 12
- Audience mix: adults, families with children and wheelchair users
- Interpretation language: English
- Interpretation content: three object records, five process records and one household note
- Physical exhibits: three empty loan utensils, F01–F03
- Display condition: one utensil beneath each lift-off acrylic cover

## Room geometry
- Internal dimensions: 6000 mm east–west × 4000 mm south–north
- Clear height: 2800 mm
- Coordinate origin: southwest internal corner
- Coordinate axes: x east; y north
- South entrance: x = 2400–3600 mm; outward-opening door
- North exit: x = 2400–3600 mm; outward-opening door
- Continuous passage: x = 2400–3600 mm; y = 0–4000 mm
- West display zone: x = 0–1800 mm; y = 600–3400 mm
- East display zone: x = 4200–6000 mm; y = 600–3400 mm
- Usable west wall length: 4000 mm
- Usable east wall length: 4000 mm
- Fixed bench footprint: x = 4600–5800 mm; y = 0–450 mm
- Fixed bench seat height: 450 mm

## Supplied display kit
| Component | Quantity | Material and dimensions | Connection or condition |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Tabletop | 2 | Birch plywood, 1200 × 600 × 18 mm | Four M6 hand knobs per top |
| Folding trestle | 4 | Steel, open height 732 mm; folded envelope 732 × 600 × 80 mm | Two trestles per top |
| Graphic frame | 2 | Aluminium, 1200 × 900 × 30 mm | Two clamps per frame; lower edge at tabletop height |
| Textile graphic | 2 | Tensioned polyester, 1200 × 900 mm | Replaceable silicone edge |
| Frame clamp | 4 | Steel, hand-operated | Two per frame |
| M6 hand knob | 8 | Steel thread, polymer grip | Four per tabletop |
| Lift-off cover | 3 | Clear acrylic, external envelope 500 × 450 × 450 mm | One utensil per cover |
| Storage crate | 2 | Internal dimensions 1250 × 950 × 950 mm | Stored outside the exhibition room during opening |

- Assembled table surface height: 750 mm
- Assembled graphic frame top height: 1650 mm
- Maximum packed-part envelope: 1200 × 900 × 450 mm
- Assembly fittings: hand knobs and frame clamps

## Interpretation dimensions
- Object-label centre height: 1000 mm above floor
- Introductory body text: 50 pt at installed size
- Object-label body text: 24 pt at installed size
- Process order: 1 Prepare; 2 Salt; 3 Pack; 4 Wait; 5 Serve
- Object associations: F01 with steps 1 and 2; F02 with step 3; F03 with steps 3, 4 and 5

## Operating states
| State label | Visitors | Doors | Graphic lighting | Objects and furniture |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Open | 12 | Both open outward | On | Three covered utensils; installed furniture positions |
| Closed | 0 | Both shut | Off | Three covered utensils; same furniture positions |

# TIME AT THE TABLE — delivery catalog

This table lists every commissioned deliverable with its tier, file format and stage. What each deliverable must contain is stated in the commission letter.

| # | id | Deliverable | Tiers | Format and stage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | exhibition-floor-plan | Final exhibition floor plan | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 2 | installation-interpretation | Installation and interpretation document | 6 | Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final. |
| 3 | south-entrance-view | Visitor perspective from the south entrance | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 4 | north-exit-view | Visitor perspective from the north exit | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 5 | open-state | Open exhibition state | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 6 | closed-state | Closed exhibition state | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |

# Object and process records

## Object register and label copy
| ID | Name | Year | Dimensions | Appearance | Label body |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F01 | Mixing bowl | 1998 | Diameter 320 mm; height 140 mm | Cream enamel bowl with a dark blue rolled rim and one small chip on the outer rim | This bowl held sliced cabbage while salt was mixed through it. On Mill Lane, preparing a batch was shared kitchen work. |
| F02 | Wooden tamper | 2004 | Length 280 mm; maximum diameter 60 mm | Pale beech tool with a straight cylindrical grip and a wider flat-ended foot | This wooden tool pressed cabbage into the jar. Its broad foot reached the vegetables while the narrow handle fitted the hand. |
| F03 | Fermentation jar | 1996 | Maximum diameter 240 mm; height including lid 360 mm | Ovoid amber-brown glazed stoneware jar with a short neck and a shallow domed lift-off lid | This lidded jar held the packed vegetables during fermentation. It stood on a kitchen shelf before portions were brought to the table. |

## Process graphic copy
| Order | Heading | Body | Associated object IDs |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Prepare | The household washed and sliced cabbage into the enamel bowl. | F01 |
| 2 | Salt | Salt was mixed through the cabbage in the bowl. | F01 |
| 3 | Pack | The cabbage moved into the jar and was pressed down with the wooden tamper. | F02, F03 |
| 4 | Wait | The covered jar remained on the kitchen shelf while the vegetables fermented. | F03 |
| 5 | Serve | Small portions were taken from the jar and served alongside the household meal. | F03 |

## Household context copy
| Heading | Body |
|---|---|
| A place in the day | On Mill Lane, a batch began with shared preparation at the kitchen table. The jar then occupied a shelf, and its contents returned to the table in small portions with meals. |

## Printed text records
| Element | Exact text |
|---|---|
| Exhibition title | TIME AT THE TABLE |
| Descriptor | Everyday work, shared food |
| Open-state label | Open |
| Closed-state label | Closed |

steps.userMessage:
TIME AT THE TABLE | A neighbourhood exhibition about everyday fermentation

We are commissioning a temporary exhibition for Riverside Community House, open from 7 to 28 November 2026. Visitors should be able to follow a household fermentation story in 5 to 8 minutes: preparing vegetables, adding salt, packing a jar, waiting and serving. The three loan objects are F01 Mixing bowl, 1998, diameter 320 mm and height 140 mm; F02 Wooden tamper, 2004, length 280 mm and diameter 60 mm; and F03 Fermentation jar, 1996, diameter 240 mm and height 360 mm. Their labels and the Mill Lane household notes are supplied in 03-object-and-process-records.en.md. Build the interpretation around these records, with the utensils as the centre of attention. Print "TIME AT THE TABLE" and "Everyday work, shared food" on the introductory graphic.

The room measures 6000 × 4000 mm, with a clear height of 2800 mm. A centred 1200 mm entrance in the south wall faces a centred 1200 mm exit in the north wall; both doors open outward. The connecting 1200 mm-wide passage runs through the room. Two display zones, each 1800 × 2800 mm, sit against the west and east walls, starting 600 mm from the south wall. Each side wall offers 4000 mm of usable length. Arrange the supplied kit within these zones: two 1200 × 600 mm birch plywood tabletops, four folding trestles, two aluminium graphic frames with two replaceable textile graphics, four frame clamps, eight M6 hand knobs and three lift-off acrylic covers. Table surfaces sit 750 mm above the floor; frame tops sit at 1650 mm. Assembly uses hand knobs and clamps. The maximum packed-part envelope is 1200 × 900 × 450 mm, with two storage crates. A fixed bench occupies the southeast corner. Plan for up to 12 visitors at once, including families and wheelchair users.

Audience: the community programme team and exhibition installer, choosing the display arrangement and preparing the room for opening.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md records the room, furniture, visitor assumptions and graphic dimensions. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the six deliverables and their proportions, formats and stages. 03-object-and-process-records.en.md supplies object identities, exact label text, five process steps and household context. room-constraint.png supplies the measured room boundary, door openings, passage, display zones and bench position. utensil-identities.png supplies the three utensils’ appearance, dimension rulers and object labels. empty-community-room.png supplies the room’s material atmosphere. community-visitors.png supplies the scale and character of a small visiting group.

Deliverables:
1. One final floor plan with named display zones, the five-step visitor route, all three objects identified by ID, name and year, furniture footprints, door openings and passage dimensions
2. One three-page installation and interpretation document: a dimensioned display elevation and furniture connection detail on page 1; the introductory graphic, five-step graphic and household note on page 2; and the three finished object labels arranged as an object catalogue on page 3
3. Two visitor perspectives of the completed exhibition, one from the south entrance and one from the north exit looking back through the room
4. Two matching overhead state drawings, one labelled "Open" with visitors and one labelled "Closed" with both doors shut and lighting off

Acceptance:
- The floor plan and both state drawings retain the 6000 × 4000 mm room, centred 1200 mm door openings, continuous 1200 mm passage, two 1800 × 2800 mm display zones and fixed southeast bench; the visitor perspectives use these same positions.
- The floor plan, installation document and visitor perspectives retain F01 Mixing bowl, 1998; F02 Wooden tamper, 2004; and F03 Fermentation jar, 1996, with the dimensions and appearances supplied. The floor plan and document repeat each complete ID, name and year together.
- Page 2 of the installation document prints TIME AT THE TABLE, Everyday work, shared food, the five step headings and bodies in their recorded order, and the household note from 03-object-and-process-records.en.md. Page 3 reproduces all three object labels, including their IDs, names, years and complete bodies. Both visitor perspectives show the same graphics in their installed positions.
- Page 1 of the installation document dimensions table surfaces at 750 mm, frame tops at 1650 mm and object-label centres at 1000 mm above the floor; pages 2 and 3 use 50 pt introductory body text and 24 pt object-label body text at installed size.
- The floor plan and installation document account for two tabletops, four trestles, two frames, two textile graphics, four clamps, eight M6 hand knobs and three acrylic covers. The connection detail identifies the hand-operated fittings, the 1200 × 900 × 450 mm packed-part limit and two storage crates.
- The Open and Closed drawings use an identical viewpoint and furniture arrangement. Open shows 12 visitors, open doors and illuminated graphics; Closed shows the doors shut and lighting off. All three utensils remain beneath their acrylic covers in both drawings.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
